fix.shows: Reuters reports that India's revision of the rolls left off or deleted 130 million names, and it says data shows the omissions fall disproportionately on Muslims. It spoke to 10 families whose relatives were detained, deported or questioned about their citizenship after their names were dropped from the rolls, and it says all of them had Indian identity or family documents while relatives, among them parents and siblings, stayed on the rolls. It reports that a woman from West Bengal, on the state's rolls since at least 2008 by the voter card Reuters saw, says she was detained in Mumbai on 19 July and forced across the border into Bangladesh, and that court filings show she was one of 149 people deported in that operation. It reports that Mumbai's Foreigners Regional Registration Office told the Calcutta High Court she had produced a Bangladeshi birth certificate and no valid or credible documentary evidence of Indian citizenship, and that she disputes this. It reports a petition in the Calcutta High Court by five people who say they were detained after their names were deleted from the rolls while their appeals were pending before the special tribunals. One of them told Reuters that police in Chhattisgarh detained him with 22 others, that 19 were released after 14 days when their names were found on the revised rolls, and that he and three others were held for 32 days. It cites the Sabar Institute for the finding that Muslims were about 70% of the 2.7 million names deleted in West Bengal after a closer review, against 27% of the population. It quotes Home Minister Amit Shah at a rally in Haryana on 5 November saying that the BJP would detect infiltrators, remove them from the rolls and expel them. It says that removal from the roll does not by itself establish that anyone is a foreigner, and that the Home Ministry, the Prime Minister's Office and the Election Commission did not respond to a request for comment.

fix.shows: Hindustan Times sets the draft rolls of the special summary revision, published on 12 November, against the final rolls of the intensive revision and reports about 50 lakh electors added across the nine states and union territories for which figures were released, with rises of 0.1% to 3%. It gives Bihar about 7.55 crore electors, about 13 lakh more than its final roll of 7.42 crore. It gives Tamil Nadu about 5.77 crore, about 10 lakh more than its final roll and below the 6.41 crore it held before the intensive revision. It gives Madhya Pradesh 8.19 lakh more for nearly 5.48 crore, Rajasthan a rise of 2.22% or about 11 lakh, and Kerala 2.736 crore against 2.695 crore, about 4.06 lakh more. It puts the largest rise in Goa, about 3%, with about 43,000 names added and at least 11,000 deleted. It gives Uttarakhand 1,25,216 names added and 6,130 applications for deletion processed, and Manipur about 33,700 more. It sets the additions beside the fall in the rolls from about 50.9 crore to 44.4 crore at the drafts of the intensive revision's second phase in 12 states and union territories, and it says applicants in the summary revision do not have to submit documents proving citizenship or be mapped to earlier rolls. It reports that Uttar Pradesh moved its draft to 17 November, that claims and objections close on 11 December and that the final rolls are due on 4 January.
